title: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed
layout_note: Four tinted panels left to right (Layer #1 opened, Pruning, collapsed Layer #N, Matching) threaded by two colour-coded rails for images A and B, with an exit gate under each layer.
grouping: Four rounded tinted panels in a row with titles above: grey for the transformer layers (Layer #1 wide and opened, Layer #N narrow and collapsed, preceded by a vertical ellipsis), pale green for Pruning and Matching. Image A's elements are blue and image B's red throughout.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles: tan for the self- and cross-attention units, grey for the confidence classifiers 'c'; circled-plus glyphs for residual additions and circled-dot glyphs for positional encoding. Inputs are two tilted parallelogram 'images' with blue and red keypoint dots; the Pruning panel repeats the parallelograms with black crosses on pruned points; Matching shows a 4x4 grey-shaded similarity matrix with a light-blue descriptor column at its left and a pink row beneath labelled 'matchability'. Door-like exit icons with grey block arrows sit below the layers with 'exit?', 'no' and 'yes!'.
proposed_highlight: The adaptive mechanisms get their own space - Pruning and Matching in pale-green panels, an exit gate under each layer answering 'no' or 'yes!' - while the repeated layer is taught once in full (Layer #1) and then collapsed to a narrow grey strip (Layer #N).
lesson: Teach a repeated layer once in full and collapse its later copy to a narrow strip showing only what changes (the confidence heads), so the space goes to the new mechanisms - exit gates and pruning - drawn between the layers.
notes: venue: unverified (the PDF carries no venue line); remembered as ICCV 2023. year = arXiv preprint year.

arrangement.units: four rounded tinted panels left to right: grey Layer #1 (opened), pale-green Pruning, narrow grey Layer #N (collapsed), pale-green Matching
arrangement.inputs_as: two tilted image parallelograms with blue (A) and red (B) keypoint dots, labelled 'local features'
arrangement.shared: each image's rail passes its own tan 'self' box, and one 'cross' box sits between the two rails, tapped by both

taxonomy.task: matching sparse local features between two images with adaptive depth and width
taxonomy.note: family other: sparse local feature matching (SuperGlue line), not covered by the family list

insights.structure: Two colour-coded rails (A blue on top, B red at the bottom) run through four tinted panels left to right; inside Layer #1 each rail passes its own self-attention box and both meet at one cross-attention box between them, and an exit gate hangs below each layer.
insights.data: Inputs are keypoint dots on image parallelograms, pruned points are black crosses on the same drawings, and the output is a similarity matrix with A's descriptor column and a pink row beneath.
insights.emphasis: The new mechanisms take space: Pruning is its own green panel drawn on the keypoints, Layer #N is shrunk to a narrow strip, and the exit decision is a black line from each confidence head down to a gate answering 'no' or 'yes!'.
insights.flow: The coloured rails are straight horizontal lines across the whole figure with short vertical taps into the attention boxes; black control lines drop from the confidence heads to the gates and turn back up into Pruning or Matching.
insights.avoid: The 'no' branch hooking back up into the Pruning panel is cramped, and the door-shaped exit icon is not readable without its 'exit?' label.

core.what: the layer stack drawn as Layer #1 opened in full, a Pruning panel, then a collapsed narrow Layer #N, each layer with an exit gate below that answers 'no' (prune and continue) or 'yes!' (go to Matching)

relations.form: A's blue rail above and B's red rail below face each other across one cross-attention box in Layer #1 and end on a similarity matrix with A's descriptor cells as a column at its left and a pink row beneath
each image's rail passes its own tan self-attention box, the two stacked one above the other in Layer #1
pruning drawn on the keypoints themselves: the image parallelograms repeated in the Pruning panel with black crosses on the dropped blue and red points
four tinted panels in one left-to-right row (Layer #1, Pruning, Layer #N, Matching) ending in an 'assignment' arrow

channels.colour: blue = image A, red = image B (dots, rails, descriptor cells; the pink row under the matrix, fed by B's rail, is labelled 'matchability'); tan = attention units; grey = confidence classifiers and the layer-panel tint; pale green = non-layer stages (Pruning, Matching); grey shading inside the matrix = similarity value
channels.shape: rounded rectangle = learned unit; circled plus = residual add; circled dot = positional encoding; parallelogram with dots = an image's keypoints; grid = similarity matrix; door icon = exit gate
channels.line: coloured arrows = per-image data; black arrows = control (confidence -> exit decision)
channels.frame: tinted rounded panel = one layer or stage; narrow panel = a collapsed repeat of the layer

quality.strengths: Data is drawn as keypoints and the matching as a matrix; one colour per image is held from inputs to output; pruning is drawn on the keypoints themselves; the repeated layer is taught once and collapsed later, so space goes to the adaptive mechanisms (exit gates, pruning); the rails are straight lines through the whole figure and control signals are separated from data by black line colour.
quality.weaknesses: The pink row under the matrix is fed by B's red rail yet labelled 'matchability', so whether it shows B's descriptors or a matchability score is unclear; the 'no' hook back into Pruning is cramped; the exit icon is cryptic without its label.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
